title: Unbounded open restriction of derived condensed-module direct image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$; all schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible [sk-def-localizing-closure], with the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories and total derived pushpull [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and exact termwise open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Let $r:W\to\overline Y$ be a morphism, $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $U=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$, and $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, $p:U\to Y$ the projections [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion]. On these unbounded derived categories the exact open adjunctions descend to $D(i_!)\dashv D(i^*)$ and $D(j_!)\dashv D(j^*)$, with invertible units $\eta_i,\eta_j$ induced termwise by the sheaf adjunctions. The open base-change isomorphism $r^*i_!\simeq j_!p^*$ induces the natural isomorphism $$\rho_B:i^*Rr_*B\xrightarrow{\sim}Rp_*j^*B\qquad(B\in D(W_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda))$$ characterized by the natural chain $$\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^*Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(i_!T,Rr_*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(r^*i_!T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(j_!p^*T,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(p^*T,j^*B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*j^*B).$$ The units, the adjunction Hom bijections and $\rho$ are compatible with the canonical shift identifications. No properness of $r$ and no boundedness or constructibility of $B$ or $T\in D(Y_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ are assumed.

source.place: Proof (2), first sentence: restriction commutes with derived direct image, with exact open adjunction and shift normalization.

proof.text: For any map $f$ in the square, [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] identifies $f^{-1}\Lambda_{\mathrm{target}}$ with $\Lambda_{\mathrm{source}}$ and makes the module pullback exact. For $h=i,j$, [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives the exact module functor $h_!$ and its adjunction with $h^*$. Its underlying sheaf adjunction is the abelian open adjunction. By [lem-sfb-finite-extension-by-zero-fully-faithful], applied with $\mathcal A=\Ab$, the abelian unit is invertible. By [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] the module adjunction $h_!\dashv h^*$ is the composite of $\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_h}\dashv\operatorname{Coext}_{\alpha_h}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_h}$, whose unit is invertible because $\alpha_h$ is a ring isomorphism, with the linearized adjunction $h^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\dashv\operatorname{mapMod}(h^*_{\Ab})$, whose unit has as underlying map the abelian unit. The latter is therefore an invertible module-linear map, and its inverse is module-linear (multiply the linearity equation on the two sides by the inverse). So the module unit is a composite of two isomorphisms. Consequently the actual units $1\to i^*i_!$ and $1\to j^*j_!$ are isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09BN, lemma-open-immersion; module linearization as in sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to each $h_!\dashv h^*$, $h=i,j$. Its unit and counit on complexes have degree-$q$ components the sheaf unit and counit. Both functors are exact, so [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] gives their unbounded derived functors and their factorization through localization at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] to these two factorizations. This produces $D(h_!)\dashv D(h^*)$, with unit and counit the localized termwise maps, under the specified composition identifications. In particular the units $\eta_i,\eta_j$ are invertible, because their termwise representatives from step 1 are invertible in every degree.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization; adjunction descent with its normalization as stated in lem-sfb-adjunction-localization

proof.text: Use [lem-sf-ring-sheaf-base-change-mates] with ambient scheme $\overline Y$, ring object $B=\Lambda_{\overline Y}$, open immersion $i$, the reduced closed complement of $Y$ as closed immersion, and $g=r$; the qcqs hypotheses hold for the finite-type separated schemes here. Its open comparison is an isomorphism $r^{-1}i^{\mathrm{sf}}_!N\cong j^{\mathrm{sf}}_!p^{\mathrm{sq}}N$ for $i^{-1}B$-modules $N$, where, by [def-sf-proetale-ring-sheaf-operations], $r^{-1}$ and $p^{-1}$ are mapMod of the abelian inverse images, $h^{\mathrm{sf}}_!$ is mapModLeft of the abelian open adjunction, and $p^{\mathrm{sq}}$ is $p^{-1}$ followed by restriction of scalars through the square coefficient isomorphism $c:j^{-1}r^{-1}B\cong p^{-1}i^{-1}B$, the component at $B$ of the inverse-image composition comparison for $rj=ip$. On the other side, [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] gives $r^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_r}\circ r^{-1}$ and $p^*=\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha_p}\circ p^{-1}$, and [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] gives $h_!=h^{\mathrm{lin}}_!\circ\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha_h}$, where $h^{\mathrm{lin}}_!$ is the same linearization of $h^{\Ab}_!$ as $h^{\mathrm{sf}}_!$. All $\alpha$'s are ring isomorphisms by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients], and $\operatorname{Ext}_{\alpha}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{\alpha^{-1}}$ by [def-sfb-modobj-extension-along-iso]. Restriction of scalars along a ring isomorphism commutes with $h^{\mathrm{lin}}_!$: both have underlying sheaf $h^{\Ab}_!M$, and the actions agree since the projection-formula isomorphism of [sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek] is natural in the ring factor.

source.place: Proof (4), construction of the arbitrary-ring open base-change comparison; exact localization expanded here

proof.text: By step 3, for $T\in\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}$ both $r^*i_!T$ and $j_!p^*T$ are identified, through the comparison of [lem-sf-ring-sheaf-base-change-mates], with $j^{\Ab}_!p^{-1}T$, the $\Lambda_U$-action on $p^{-1}T$ being obtained through the ring isomorphisms $\varphi_1=\alpha_j\circ j^{-1}(\alpha_r)\circ c^{-1}$, resp. $\varphi_2=\alpha_p\circ p^{-1}(\alpha_i)$, from $p^{-1}i^{-1}\Lambda_{\overline Y}$ to $\Lambda_U$. These agree. Indeed $\alpha_f$ is built from the inverse-image composition comparisons ([sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]), $\eta_f$ is its mate, and [lem-sfb-eta-comp] gives $\eta_{rj}=c_{j,r}\circ r_*(\eta_j)\circ\eta_r$ and $\eta_{ip}=c_{p,i}\circ i_*(\eta_p)\circ\eta_i$. Since $rj=ip$ is one morphism $U\to\overline Y$, these two composites are equal. Taking mates, and using that $c$ is the composite of the two inverse-image composition comparisons for $rj$ and $ip$, gives $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$. Hence the comparison is $\Lambda_W$-linear, natural in $T$, and is an isomorphism $\beta:r^*i_!\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!p^*$ of functors $\Mod_{\Lambda_Y}\to\Mod_{\Lambda_W}$. Every factor is exact by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] and [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition] to obtain the natural isomorphism $D(r^*)D(i_!)\cong D(j_!)D(p^*)$ on all unbounded objects, induced termwise by $\beta$.

source.place: Proof (4), construction of the arbitrary-ring open base-change comparison; exact localization expanded here

proof.text: For each scheme $V$ here, [lem-sfb-proetale-sheaves-grothendieck] with $\mathcal A=\Ab$ gives that $\Sh(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Ab)$ is Grothendieck abelian. The closed additive symmetric monoidal tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] permits [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] to apply to its commutative ring object $\Lambda_V$. Thus the module category is Grothendieck abelian, so has unbounded K-injective resolutions by [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. By [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] the adjunctions for $r$ and $p$ are $Lr^*\dashv Rr_*$ and $Lp^*\dashv Rp_*$, with $Rr_*,Rp_*$ the K-injective total derived functors. The exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] identifies $Lr^*,Lp^*$ with $D(r^*),D(p^*)$, since step 1 established exactness. In the chain use the canonical adjunctions $D(r^*)\dashv Rr_*$ and $D(p^*)\dashv Rp_*$ of [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift] (exact additive left adjoints, K-injective resolutions in the target). Step 8 uses the same adjunctions. For fixed $B$ and arbitrary $T$, compose the Hom bijection of step 2 for $i$, the derived $r$-adjunction, precomposition with $\beta_T^{-1}$ from step 4, the Hom bijection for $j$, and the derived $p$-adjunction. This gives exactly the five bijections in the statement, in that order. Denote their composite by $\Phi_{T,B}:\operatorname{Hom}(T,i^*Rr_*B)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(T,Rp_*j^*B)$. Each factor is natural in both variables, hence so is $\Phi$.

source.place: Proof (2), first sentence: restriction commutes with derived direct image, with exact open adjunction and shift normalization.

proof.text: Put $X_B=i^*Rr_*B$ and $Z_B=Rp_*j^*B$. Define $\rho_B=\Phi_{X_B,B}(1_{X_B})$ and $\sigma_B=\Phi^{-1}_{Z_B,B}(1_{Z_B})$. Naturality in $T$ gives $\Phi_{T,B}(a)=\rho_Ba$ and $\Phi^{-1}_{T,B}(b)=\sigma_Bb$. Applying these identities to $a=1_{X_B}$ and $b=1_{Z_B}$ yields $\sigma_B\rho_B=1_{X_B}$ and $\rho_B\sigma_B=1_{Z_B}$. Thus $\rho_B$ is an isomorphism. Naturality in $B$ gives $\rho_{B'}X(u)=Z(u)\rho_B$ for every $u:B\to B'$. The first displayed identity also proves the required characterization and uniqueness: any map inducing the same Hom chain equals $\Phi_{X_B,B}(1_{X_B})$. This is the explicit representing-map argument, using only the bijections already constructed.

source.place: Proof (2), first sentence: restriction commutes with derived direct image, with exact open adjunction and shift normalization.

proof.text: The exact functors in steps 1--4 use the shifts of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. On complexes their degree-$q$ shift comparisons are identities on the objects in degree $q+n$; additivity changes the shifted differential to $(-1)^nF(d)$. Therefore for any natural transformation $a$ of these additive functors, the maps $C(a)_{K[n]}$ and $C(a)_K[n]$ agree in every degree. Apply this to the open units, counits, and $\beta$, and to the identity composition comparisons. The termwise adjunction formulas of [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and the unit/counit formulas of [lem-sfb-adjunction-localization] show that their descended maps have the same shift squares. For $D(\beta)$ and composition use the uniqueness with the termwise normalization in [lem-sfb-exact-derived-natural-iso] and [lem-sfb-exact-derived-composition]. This proves shift compatibility of $\eta_i,\eta_j$, the open adjunction bijections, and the middle base-change bijection, with the prescribed shifts.

source.place: Proof (2), first sentence: restriction commutes with derived direct image, with exact open adjunction and shift normalization.

proof.text: For $r^*\dashv r_*$ and $p^*\dashv p_*$ use [lem-sp-canonical-right-derived-adjunction-shift]. Its hypotheses hold: the module functors are additive, the left adjoints are exact by step 1, and step 5 established the unbounded K-injective resolution hypotheses of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] for these module categories. The cited lemma preserves the canonical K-injective shift, and makes these derived adjunction units and counits shift-compatible. Hence the other two Hom bijections of step 5 commute with simultaneous shift of $T$ and $B$. Together with step 7 every factor of $\Phi$ does. If $s_X:X_{B[n]}\xrightarrow{\sim}X_B[n]$ and $s_Z:Z_{B[n]}\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_B[n]$ are the canonical composite shifts, apply this compatibility to $1_{X_B}$ shifted by $n$. The defining equation of step 6 gives $s_Z\rho_{B[n]}=\rho_B[n]s_X$. This is the asserted shift square for $\rho$. None of the constructions used a cohomological bound, constructibility, or properness of $r$.
